newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai stocks end down on bank and finance sales.
newsitem.headline: Thai stocks end down on bank and finance sales.

text.p: Thai stocks ended down on Monday as buying by mutual funds operating a market support fund failed to counter underlying sales pressure on bank and finance stocks, dealers said.
The SET Index closed down 5.28 points, or 0.74 percent, to 708.20. The SET 50 closed down 0.42 points, or 0.81 percent, to 51.65. Turnover was 4.44 billion baht.
"The mutual funds were buying into the telecoms sector, not into the banks or finance stocks which were heavily sold," said a trader at Phatra Thanakit.
"The banks and finance companies are seen as having a lot of bad loans," he said.

Finance stocks lost 4.95 percent as investors remained concerned that firms' rising borrowing costs and deteriorating asset quality will dampen earnings and could lead to possible instability in the sector, traders said.
Telecoms stocks gained from Thailand signing of a 68 nation World Trade Organisation liberalisation pact, dealers said.
Following a morning roller coaster, buying in the telecoms sector helped keep the index in a narrow range during the afternoon session. Communications stocks gained 1.31 percent.

Corporate profits reported by energy firms Cogeneration and Banpu were in line with market expectations while a 55 million baht third quarter loss by Bangkok Land had been widely anticipated, dealers said.
"I think the energy results are quite positive, but expected by most ... Personally I think the general market outlook is not so good even if figures are," he said.
Among the active bank sector Siam Commercial shed seven to 130, and Bangkok Bank lost one to 167. In telecoms Jasmine added 1.75 to 34, and TelecomAsia which put on 2.25 baht to 48.25.
